--------
In this VladTV interview, former Delta Force operator Dale Comstock discusses whether elite military training could help someone evade modern law enforcement inside the United States. Responding to Vlad’s question about surveillance, cameras, cell phones, triangulation and tracking technology, Comstock says he believes it is still possible, despite what he describes as a rapidly expanding “surveillance state.” He breaks down concerns around Flock cameras, hidden camera systems, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cell phone data, facial recognition, gait recognition and biometrics, while warning that AI, super AI and quantum AI could make these tools even more powerful if abused. Comstock also explains his “Human Operating System” and “Sovereign Operating System,” which he says teach analog methods for preserving personal agency outside the digital world. The conversation explores privacy, technology, security, government overreach and the limits of modern tracking in America.

--------
Robinhood co-founder and CEO Vlad Tenev sits down with DJ Vlad to trace the fintech company’s rise after its 2015 launch, from early conversations and missed investment opportunities to major Silicon Valley funding rounds. Tenev explains how DST Global, Yuri Milner’s firm, backed Robinhood through multiple rounds, valuing the company at $1.3 billion in 2017, $5.6 billion in 2018, $7.5 billion in 2019, and around $15 billion in 2020—when his stake pushed him into billionaire territory on paper.

The conversation also covers Robinhood’s role in popularizing commission-free stock trading, forcing legacy firms like Fidelity and Merrill Lynch to respond, and how the app became synonymous with free trades. Tenev reflects on co-founder Baiju Bhatt stepping back as co-CEO in 2020 to become chief creative officer as Robinhood prepared for its IPO and entered a new phase of legal, operational, and product growth.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Vincent Marino breaks down his two-year experience at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey, the federal facility Vlad notes is where Diddy is currently serving time. Marino explains the differences between the East and West sides, describes the prison’s large sex offender population, and says the lack of cameras can make the compound unpredictable. He also discusses the prevalence of cell phones, knives, commissary money, and “steel” inside, while detailing how masked stickup crews allegedly targeted inmates for phones, jewelry, and other valuables. Marino adds that Fort Dix can run smoothly if inmates understand the politics, but warns that the summer heat, no air conditioning, and blind spots create real risks.

Watch the full conversation for firsthand insight into federal prison life, Fort Dix conditions, inmate politics, and the Diddy-related headlines drawing new attention to the facility.
